message:
fix(np-impl r2, Codex N1): a scheduled relay reply goes only while its own record is still the current one

relayScheduleReply's timers checked only that the relay socket existed. A connect replaced within its
early replies -- by a newer connect from the same wire tuple, which nothing forbids -- went on sending
at 120/240 ms into the newer connect's legacy race, ahead of that connect's grace. Every scheduled
reply (early or after the grace) now checks, when it is due, that the eligibility record that
scheduled it is still the current one for the wire IP and unexpired; otherwise it is dropped and
logged. A replaced client keeps punching and is answered under the record that replaced it.

Tests: relay_reply_fence_test (the function from server.js on a virtual clock: replaced at 50 ms on
the same tuple / another tuple, expiry between replies, swept record, legacy replaced, undisturbed
early and legacy) -- 9 PASS, 7 FAIL against c803768's server; relay_early_test same-tuple case on a
real server -- PASS x3, afterB=2 FAIL against c803768's server.
Wording (Codex 1-2): replay's measured set is the PC viewer's 9 (same T0); host 482 and the phone's
554/626 are references; the relay replay is a synthetic input. version>=2 is a policy range, not a
future-compatibility claim.

Product: server.js (relay reply fence). Tests: fence test, relay_early, punch_any labels.
Docs: README, history, rendezvous header comment.
